A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SynOOD and have 11 readable pages containing the same research work, equations, five tables and four figures. All pages were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original SynOOD benchmark evaluations, component ablations, training-strategy comparisons and synthetic-data analyses in Section 4, Tables 1–5 and Figures 3–4.

after.justification: v3 retains the original SynOOD experimental results and analyses in Section 4, Tables 1–5 and Figures 3–4.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.5 retain the same iterative OOD image generation, noise updates, image projection training and negative-label feature tuning. No algorithm component, objective or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-1k with iNaturalist, SUN, Places365 and Texture, plus the same OpenOOD near-OOD and far-OOD datasets. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 1–3. In particular, CSP and AdaNeg already appear alongside NegLabel in v1 Table 1; v3 does not introduce them as new baselines.

E3.justification: Both versions retain the same AUROC/FPR95 evaluation, 50k-image training subset, backbone comparisons, synthetic-sample sweep and training settings. Section 4.1 and the experimental table captions are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the same generation and component ablations, synthetic-data quantity analysis, backbone comparison, joint-versus-separate training study and synthetic-image examples in Section 4.3, Tables 3–5 and Figures 3–4.

E5.justification: Both report the same point estimates and averages across datasets. Neither provides repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports average AUROC/FPR95 of 97.01/14.27 for SynOOD and 94.21/25.40 for NegLabel in both versions. The gains omitted from v3's abstract remain in the introduction and Section 4.2.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(14), including the detection setup, diffusion equations, gradient approximation and training losses, are unchanged. No mathematical definition, derivation, assumption or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The novelty, state-of-the-art performance and low-overhead claims retain their meaning and scope. Although v3's abstract omits the stated 2.80% AUROC improvement and 11.13% FPR95 reduction, both claims remain in the introduction's contribution list and Section 4.2.

C2.justification: The explanations of boundary alignment, performance decline beyond 50k synthetic samples, negative-label balance and possible projection-layer overfitting are unchanged. No substantive interpretation or limitation is added or removed.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same models, generation settings, optimizers, learning rates, epochs, batch size, hardware and image-selection procedure. The abstract's code-availability sentence is reworded, but the repository address and availability statement remain the same.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 66 references are unchanged in substance. SynOOD's positioning relative to CLIP-based detection, negative-label methods and outlier synthesis remains the same.

P1.justification: v3 shortens the abstract by deleting the numerical performance-gain phrase and revises 'Codes are available in' to 'the code is available at.' Apart from the version/date stamp, the remaining prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The shorter abstract produces local text reflow on pages 1–3 and a small upward shift of Figure 1. Figure and table contents, captions and styling remain unchanged; pages 4–11 render identically.

improvement.justification: v3 makes a small editorial revision to the abstract, reducing repetition while removing quantitative detail that remains in the introduction and Section 4.2. The method, experimental evidence, interpretations and reproducibility information are unchanged, leaving no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
